reasons.reader_question: The beat's question lands, and Chathu pocketing the unburned intake slip with his thumb over it adds a sharp new one. Ammu's fate is left a hair ambiguous ('It stopped.'), which blurs the question.
reasons.change: Every axis moves. She goes from cageable to uncageable and rogue, from witnessed to self-witnessed, and from sister to bereaved, and the wound-share already bites.
reasons.romance_movement: The reason is new: she makes him the only witness, and he strikes for her and 'did not look sorry'. His reaction to being made her one key gets only a closed-eye heartbeat and never comes back up.
reasons.shown_chemistry: Strong responsive beats carry it: 'Then I'll look harder', the hand that 'did not grip. It rested.', and her lying across him counting his heart. The best of these is undercut by a line that isn't true for him.
reasons.character_logic: Three things are convenient. Chathu leaves the caged member alone with the sister he is punishing. A man who was grey and ash-lipped minutes ago rolls inside a bear's swing. Ammu turns jackal with no resin shown after she set the pot down in the kennel.
reasons.stakes_and_cost: The stay-or-follow choice is brutal and well built. She weighs Ammu against his wound in her own ribs, chooses, hates it, and pays with Ammu's death.
reasons.prose: The prose is clean, concrete and readable, with good short-sentence impact. Door and shutter imagery is overused ('closed door', 'shutting a door', 'door shut', 'door scraped', 'slammed shutter'), and similes cluster in the bear fight. Stock lines include 'running before she knew it' and 'knew it the way she knew her own name'. Two consecutive paragraph-opener pairs start 'She' and 'He'.
reasons.continuity: Devan says 'I've watched you change every night since our wedding.' This conflicts with F125 (ten times by ch13), with the cache turnings and the many skipped-resin nights (F129, F183, F192), and with his never-lies, exact-facts voice.

fixes: Fix the continuity break at "I've watched you change every night since our wedding." Devan is literal and never lies to her, and the record says he watched about ten times by ch13, after which she turned at the cache. Replace it with an exact, true line in his voice, such as "I've watched every turning you let me see. I never once looked away." This keeps the romantic payload and the callback.

Repair the convenient recovery at "Devan was on one elbow. He had been dying minutes ago." Right now the antidote acts like a switch (irrational behaviour to extend plot). Keep him unable to stand. Let the bear's own charge bring the shoulder to him, so he strikes once from his knees in the mud and pitches forward afterward. Give one beat of him choosing to strike: his hand lifts, hesitates on the eight years, then lands. That way the first blow reads as a decision, not reflex.

Set up Ammu's turning at "Ammu was already gone. She was a shadow". She set the resin pot down in the kennel straw, so her jackal shape currently has no source (convenient magic). Have her take two fingers of resin from the pot before they leave the kennel and smear her throat as she goes. Or have Neela see her dip into the pot at the cook-house corner. Then, after "It stopped.", add one concrete sensory certainty, such as the smell of jackal blood carried back on the wind, so the loss is unambiguous (technique 19).
reader_question: With Ammu likely dead, Neela rogue and bound in wounds to a half-poisoned man, and Chathu holding the slip that carries her birth name, what is left of them at first light?
new_facts_assessment: new-facts.json is empty, but the draft adds several facts. Muthu came on horseback, not by cart, and held the arch. Ammu stole Pachan's key and the vial from Chathu's sleeve and carries a blade in her braid. Ammu learned the loophole at fourteen from a drunk master. The tappers' verse is the loophole. The vial is only partly full. The bear has a torn ear. Most important, the intake slip survives unburned, reads 'Intake, sold at six years', and Chathu keeps it. This is consistent with F012 and sets up B2 ch20, and it must be logged. The horse change is useful and quietly feeds Muthu's ambiguity. The half-empty vial and the torn ear are unexplained and should be cut or set up. The witness entry burning when Chathu reads it, rather than at the moment of self-naming, follows the beat. It loosely fits the bible's 'burns where it lies' and should be fixed in canon as 'the entry burns when next it is read or touched at night'. Otherwise keep the burning simultaneous with her word in later references.
